name: write-adr
description: Architectural Decision Record skills for the adg CLI: write-lean-adr (authoring lean records) and follow-adr-governance (obeying lean ADR briefs while changing code). Bundles Claude Code hooks: a SessionStart check that prompts to update adg when the CLI lags the plugin (and warns when the repo's allowlist is missing the Bash(adg:*) rule the agent hooks need), the whole-corpus brief at SessionStart and at Plan-subagent dispatch, the per-context-deduped file-scoped brief before an edit (session, or subagent within it — each fresh subagent gets its own first injection), a staged-file advisory before a git commit (flag-tolerant detection, git -c included) that blocks on a forbidden-scope hit, a guard that blocks hand-creating an ADR record (and warns on editing one), a commit-time judge agent that denies a commit whose staged code clearly violates a governing ADR (fail-open otherwise; cited reason fed back), a PostToolUse reviewer agent that judges an edited ADR record against the lean rubric, and a UserPromptSubmit router that points the agent at the write-adr skills whenever a prompt mentions ADRs (requires adg on PATH). As of 3.0.0, lean is the sole ADR format and adg keeps no global user state: the write-madr-adr skill, the MADR authoring lifecycle, ~/.adgconfig.yaml, and the set-config/reset-config commands are retired; the model path is the docs/decisions convention (--model per invocation), and migration is by re-authoring a record with `adg lean new`. Every accepted lean record requires a `## Why` (the reasoning) — a required section co-equal with Decision and Guidance, kept record-only so it never enters a brief and injection stays low-token. Ships with ad-guidance-tool so the guidance tracks the tool's CLI in lockstep.
